h1: Embrace Reformed Truths at Saving Grace Bible Church, Melbourne
lede: At Saving Grace Bible Church, we aim to exalt the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and magnify the truths of Scripture in the heart of Melbourne, Victoria. We stand as a steadfast lighthouse of Christ-centered reformed theology, embracing the principles of Calvinism and the profound beauty of TULIP with unwavering devotion.

blocks.text: **Our Foundation in Christ:** Our church is built upon the unshakable foundation of Christ's redemptive work. As believers, we are captivated by the grace and truth found in the Gospel. Guided by the Holy Spirit, we delve into the sacred pages of Scripture, seeking to uncover it's hidden treasures and apply it's timeless wisdom to our lives.

**Rooted in Reformed Truths:** Saving Grace is a fellowship of believers who cherish the rich tapestry of reformed theology. With a deep reverence for God's sovereignty, we embrace the teachings of Calvinism as a means of understanding His infinite majesty and the depth of His love for us.
TULIP and the Gospel Story
The petals of TULIP guide us through the symphony of God's redemptive plan:

items: **Total Depravity:** We humbly acknowledge our fallen nature, recognising our desperate need for the Savior's redeeming grace.
**Unconditional Election:** Our salvation is a testament to God's unmerited favour, a divine choice that He made before the foundation of the world.
**Limited Atonement:** Christ's sacrifice, a masterpiece of love, is efficacious for all who believe, securing their eternal inheritance.
**Irresistible Grace:** God's grace, like a gentle current, draws His chosen one's into His embrace, transforming hearts and lives.
**Perseverance of the Saints:** The saints, held in the palm of His hand, are kept by His unwavering faithfulness throughout their journey.

blocks.text: Exploring Dispensational Wisdom

While our hearts are anchored in Christ-centered reformed theology, we also humbly engage with differing perspectives, such as dispensationalism. Our commitment is to unity in Christ and the diligent study of Scripture, understanding that its multifaceted truths reveal the glory of our Creator.

**Join Us on the Journey:** We invite you to walk alongside us in worship, study, and fellowship. As we gather on Sundays for the Lord’s Day service, mornings and evenings, along with other gatherings throughout the week, we lift our voices in praise, open the Scriptures with reverence, and cultivate a more profound love for our Savior. Whether you're well-acquainted with reformed theology or are just beginning to explore its depths, there's a place for you in our Christ-centered community.

At Saving Grace Bible Church, Christ is the cornerstone of all we do, and the Scriptures are our guiding light. If you find yourself in Westmeadows or its neighbouring areas, we extend a warm invitation to experience the transformative power of Christ-centered reformed teaching.
Join us as we journey deeper into the heart of God through His Word. Let's walk hand in hand, following the footsteps of our Savior at Saving Grace Bible Church.

**Location:** We're conveniently situated at Unit 5/217-219 Mickleham Rd, Westmeadows VIC 3049. For enquiries or additional information, please feel free to reach out at [0450 545 589](tel:+61450545589) or email us at [info@savinggrace.org.au](mailto:info@savinggrace.org.au)

lede: At Saving Grace Bible Church, our mission is to glorify God by faithfully proclaiming the gospel of Jesus Christ. Guided by the Spirit and grounded in Scripture, we long to see sinners brought to salvation and believers strengthened in faith.

blocks.text: Every Sunday, we gather around God’s Word with reverence, simplicity, and joy — because Christ is worthy of true worship, and His people need the nourishment of His truth.
Service Times

items: Morning Service: 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
Evening Service: 5:30 PM - 7:00 PM

blocks.text: Order of Worship
Our worship is simple, Scripture-centred, and Christ-focused. A typical service includes…

items: Singing psalms and hymns, together in prayer
Public reading of God’s Word
Corporate Prayer
The Lord’s Supper
Expository preaching that proclaims Christ

blocks.text: Whether you are a believer seeking a faithful church home, or someone still exploring the truth of the gospel, you are warmly invited to hear God’s Word with us.
Practical Details

items: Parking: Ample parking is available.
Children: A children’s program is provided during the evening service.

blocks.text: Contact Us

For more information or if you have any questions, feel free to contact our church office on [+61 450 545 589](tel:+61450545589). You can also enquire about upcoming services through our [contact us page](/contact-us-2/).
Biblically Grounded Preaching

Each Sunday morning, Pastor Wesam Saad, a seasoned and passionate servant of God, delivers sermons deep into the Scriptures. With wisdom and clarity, our Pastor imparts biblical insights that inspire and challenge us to live out our faith practically. Our Elder Ralph Gambardella also takes turns delivering sermons on Sunday mornings, ensuring a diverse range of perspectives rooted in the Word of God.

Whether you're seeking spiritual nourishment, missed a service, or wish to revisit the teachings, these recordings serve as a valuable resource for your growth.

blocks.text: In the evenings, we meet in a relaxed setting to reflect on the morning’s sermon, ask questions, and talk about how God’s Word applies in practice.

"and let us consider how to stimulate one another to love and good deeds, not forsaking our own assembling together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another; and all the more as you see the day drawing near." Hebrews 10:24-25
Evangelistic Sermons: A Call to Salvation

We're excited to announce a new addition to our Sunday evening services: 25-minute evangelistic sermons. These sermons have a singular purpose - to call individuals to repentance and faith in Jesus for their salvation.
Our ultimate aim is to make Jesus known to all people. He is the source of hope, redemption, and everlasting life. Join us as we proclaim His name and extend His invitation to all who will listen.
Delving Deeper into the Morning's Sermon

At the heart of our Sunday Evening Service, we delve deeper into the morning's sermon message. During this service, we take the teachings and insights shared earlier in the day and explore them further, examining how they apply to our daily lives. This in-depth discussion and reflection help us understand the Word of God and apply it practically, ensuring that the power of God's grace continues to work in our hearts and minds throughout the week.
Testimonies of God's Amazing Grace

A cherished part of our Sunday Evening Service involves personal testimonies. One of our fellow brothers or sisters shares a testimony of how God's amazing grace has touched their lives, bringing about transformative change. Through these testimonies, we're reminded of the living and active presence of God in our midst.
Learning to Evangelize with Passion and Purpose

In addition to our exploration of the morning's sermon message, our Sunday Evening Service also dedicates time to the vital mission of evangelism. We understand that sharing the Good News of Jesus Christ is essential to our faith journey.

During this part of our service, we equip ourselves with the tools and knowledge needed to evangelise with passion and purpose. Whether you are new to sharing your faith or a seasoned evangelist, there is always room to grow and improve in this vital ministry.
Corporate Prayer

During our service, we set aside dedicated moments for corporate prayer, allowing us to lift our voices together in unity. We intercede for our congregation, our community, and the world, lifting up our church family's needs, concerns, and praises. This collective communion with God deepens our connection to one another and strengthens our bond as a body of believers.
Fellowship and Shared Meals

After a time of reflection and inspiration, we gather to share a meal together. This fellowship over food fosters a sense of unity and community, allowing us to build deeper relationships and create lasting connections with one another. Breaking bread together is a beautiful reminder of our unity in Christ and our shared faith journey.

blocks.text: **We believe** that the Bible is the inspired and the only infallible and authoritative Word of God. The Bible is God’s written revelation to man. It is verbally inspired in every word and absolutely inerrant in the original documents.
**We believe** that there is one God who is eternally existent in three persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit each deserving worship and adoration.

**We believe** in the deity of the Lord Jesus Christ, in His virgin birth, in His sinless life, in His miracles, in His vicarious and atoning death through His shed blood, in His bodily resurrection, in His ascension to the right hand of the Father, and in His personal return in power and glory.

**We believe** that the salvation of man, who is sinful and lost, is instantaneous, and is accomplished solely by the power of the Holy Spirit through the instrumentality of the Holy Scriptures when the repentant sinner – enabled by the Holy Spirit – responds in faith. This salvation is wholly by God’s grace on the basis of Jesus Christ’s redeeming work and the merit of His shed blood, and not on human merit or works. All of the redeemed are kept by God’s power and thus are secure in Christ forever.

**We believe** in the Spirit-filled life. The believer, being fully consecrated, is indwelt by the Holy Spirit at the moment of salvation, and thereby is enabled to witness with power to the saving of souls. That same indwelling Holy Spirit empowers believers to serve, and seals them unto the day of redemption.
**We believe** in the bodily resurrection of both the saved and the unsaved, they that are saved unto the resurrection of life, and they that are lost unto the resurrection of damnation.

**We believe** in the spiritual unity of all believers in our Lord Jesus Christ. All who declare true faith in Jesus Christ are immediately placed by the Holy Spirit into one united spiritual Body, the Church, of which Christ is the head. The purpose of the Church is to glorify God by building up its members in the faith, by instruction of the Word, by fellowship, by keeping the ordinances, and by advancing and communicating the Gospel to the whole world. The Church was initiated on the Day of Pentecost and will be completed at the coming of Christ for His own at the rapture.

blocks.text: The Holy Scriptures

We teach that the Bible is God’s written revelation to man, and thus the sixty-six books of the Bible given to us by the Holy Spirit constitute the plenary (inspired equally in all parts) Word of God ([1 Corinthians 2:7-14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%202.7-14); [2 Peter 1:20-21](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Pet%201.20-21)).

We teach that the Word of God is an objective, propositional revelation ([1 Thessalonians 2:13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Thess%202.13); [1 Corinthians 2:13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%202.13)), verbally inspired in every word ([2 Timothy 3:16](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Tim%203.16)), absolutely inerrant in the original documents, infallible, and God-breathed.

We teach the literal, grammatical, historical interpretation of Scripture which affirms the belief that the opening chapters of Genesis present creation in six literal days ([Genesis 1:31](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Gen%201.31); [Exodus 31:17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Exod%2031.17)), describe the special creation of man and woman ([Genesis 1:26-28](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Gen%201.26-28); [2:5-25](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Genesis%202.5-25)), and define marriage as between one man and one woman ([Genesis 2:24](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Gen%202.24); [Matthew 19:5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2019.5)). Scripture elsewhere dictates that any sexual activity outside of marriage is an abomination before the Lord ([Exodus 20:14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Exod%2020.14); [Leviticus 18:1-30](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Lev%2018.1-30); [Matthew 5:27-32](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%205.27-32); [19:1-9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matthew%2019.1-9); [1 Corinthians 5:1-5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%205.1-5); [6:9-10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Corinthians%206.9-10); [1 Thessalonians. 4:1-7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Thess.%204.1-7)).

We teach that the Bible constitutes the only infallible rule of faith and practice ([Matthew 5:18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%205.18); [24:35](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matthew%2024.35); [John 10:35](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2010.35); [16:12-13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2016.12-13); [17:17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2017.17); [1 Corinthians 2:13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%202.13); [2 Timothy 3:15-17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Tim%203.15-17); [Hebrews 4:12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%204.12); [2 Peter 1:20-21](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Pet%201.20-21)).

We teach that God spoke in His written Word by a process of dual authorship. The Holy Spirit so superintended the human authors that, through their individual personalities and different styles of writing, they composed and recorded God’s Word to man ([2 Peter 1:20-21](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Pet%201.20-21)) without error in the whole or in the part ([Matthew 5:18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%205.18); [2 Timothy 3:16](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Tim%203.16)).

We teach that, whereas there may be several applications of any given passage of Scripture, there is but one true interpretation. The meaning of Scripture is to be found as one diligently applies the literal, grammatical, historical method of interpretation under the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit ([John 7:17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%207.17); [16:12-15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2016.12-15); [1 Corinthians 2:7-15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%202.7-15); [1 John 2:20](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20John%202.20)). It is the responsibility of believers to ascertain carefully the true intent and meaning of Scripture, recognizing that proper application is binding on all generations. Yet the truth of Scripture stands in judgment of men; never do men stand in judgment of it.
God

We teach that there is but one living and true God ([Deuteronomy 6:4](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Deut%206.4); [Isaiah 45:5-7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Isa%2045.5-7); [1 Corinthians 8:4](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%208.4)), an infinite, all-knowing Spirit ([John 4:24](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%204.24)), perfect in all His attributes, one in essence, eternally existing in three Persons—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit ([Matthew 28:19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2028.19); [2 Corinthians 13:14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%2013.14))—each equally deserving worship and obedience.

**God the Father.** We teach that God the Father, the first Person of the Trinity, orders and disposes all things according to His own purpose and grace ([Psalm 145:8-9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ps%20145.8-9); [1 Corinthians 8:6](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%208.6)). He is the Creator of all things ([Genesis 1:1-31](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Gen%201.1-31); [Ephesians 3:9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%203.9)). As the only absolute and omnipotent Ruler in the universe, He is sovereign in creation, providence, and redemption ([Psalm 103:19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ps%20103.19); [Romans 11:36](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%2011.36)). His fatherhood involves both His designation within the Trinity and His relationship with mankind. As Creator He is Father to all men ([Ephesians 4:6](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%204.6)), but He is spiritual Father only to believers ([Romans 8:14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%208.14); [2 Corinthians 6:18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%206.18)). He has decreed for His own glory all things that come to pass ([Ephesians 1:11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%201.11)). He continually upholds, directs, and governs all creatures and events ([1 Chronicles 29:11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Chron%2029.11)). In His sovereignty He is neither the author nor approver of sin ([Habakkuk 1:13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Hab%201.13); [John 8:38-47](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%208.38-47)), nor does He abridge the accountability of moral, intelligent creatures ([1 Peter 1:17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Pet%201.17)). He has graciously chosen from eternity past those whom He would have as His own ([Ephesians 1:4-6](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%201.4-6)); He saves from sin all who come to Him through Jesus Christ; He adopts as His own all those who come to Him; and He becomes, upon adoption, Father to His own ([John 1:12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%201.12); [Romans 8:15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%208.15); [Galatians 4:5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Gal%204.5); [Hebrews 12:5-9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%2012.5-9)).

**God the Son.** We teach that Jesus Christ, the second Person of the Trinity, possesses all the divine excellencies, and in these He is coequal, consubstantial, and coeternal with the Father ([John 10:30](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2010.30); [14:9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2014.9)).

We teach that God the Father created according to His own will, through His Son, Jesus Christ, by whom all things continue in existence and in operation ([John 1:3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%201.3); [Colossians 1:15-17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Col%201.15-17); [Hebrews 1:2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%201.2)).

We teach that in the incarnation the eternal Son, the second Person of the Trinity, without altering His divine nature or surrendering any of the divine attributes, made Himself of no reputation by taking on a full human nature consubstantial with our own, yet without sin ([Philippians 2:5-8](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Phil%202.5-8); [Hebrews 4:15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%204.15); [7:26](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Hebrews%207.26)).

We teach that He was conceived by the Holy Spirit in the womb of the virgin Mary ([Luke 1:35](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Luke%201.35)) and thus born of a woman ([Galatians 4:4-5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Gal%204.4-5)), so that two whole, perfect, and distinct natures, the divine and the human, were joined together in one person, without confusion, change, division, or separation. He is therefore very God and very man, yet one Christ, the only mediator between God and man.

We teach that in His incarnation, Christ fully possessed His divine nature, attributes, and prerogatives ([Colossians 2:9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Col%202.9); cf. [Luke 5:18-26](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Luke%205.18-26); [John 16:30](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2016.30); [20:28](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2020.28)). However, in the state of His humiliation, He did not always fully express the glories of His majesty, concealing them behind the veil of His genuine humanity ([Matthew 17:2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2017.2); [Mark 13:32](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Mark%2013.32); [Philippians 2:5-8](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Phil%202.5-8)). According to His human nature, He acts in submission to the Father ([John 4:34](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%204.34); [5:19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%205.19), [30](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%205.30); [6:38](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%206.38)) by the power of Holy Spirit ([Isaiah 42:1](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Isa%2042.1); [Matthew 12:28](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2012.28); [Luke 4:1](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Luke%204.1), [14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Luke%204.14)), while, according to His divine nature, He acts by His authority and power as the eternal Son ([John 1:14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%201.14); cf. [2:11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%202.11); [10:37–38](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2010.37%E2%80%9338); [14:10–11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2014.10%E2%80%9311)).

We teach that our Lord Jesus Christ accomplished our redemption through the shedding of His blood and sacrificial death on the cross and that His death was voluntary, vicarious, substitutionary, propitiatory, and redemptive ([John 10:15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2010.15); [Romans 3:24-25](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%203.24-25); [5:8](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Romans%205.8); [1 Peter 2:24](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Pet%202.24)).

We teach that on the basis of the efficacy of the death of our Lord Jesus Christ, the believing sinner is freed from the punishment, the penalty, the power, and one day the very presence of sin; and that he is declared righteous, given eternal life, and adopted into the family of God ([Romans 3:25](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%203.25); [5:8-9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Romans%205.8-9); [2 Corinthians 5:14-15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%205.14-15); [1 Peter 2:24](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Pet%202.24); [3:18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Peter%203.18)).

We teach that our justification is made sure by His literal, physical resurrection from the dead and that He is now ascended to the right hand of the Father, where He now mediates as our Advocate and High Priest ([Matthew 28:6](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2028.6); [Luke 24:38-39](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Luke%2024.38-39); [Acts 2:30-31](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%202.30-31); [Romans 4:25](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%204.25); [8:34](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Romans%208.34); [Hebrews 7:25](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%207.25); [9:24](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Hebrews%209.24); [1 John 2:1](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20John%202.1)).

We teach that in the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the grave, God confirmed the deity of His Son and gave proof that God has accepted the atoning work of Christ on the cross. Jesus’ bodily resurrection is also the guarantee of a future resurrection life for all believers ([John 5:26-29](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%205.26-29); [14:19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2014.19); [Romans 1:4](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%201.4); [4:25](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Romans%204.25); [6:5-10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Romans%206.5-10); [1 Corinthians 15:20](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2015.20), [23](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Corinthians%2015.23)).

We teach that Jesus Christ will return to receive the church, which is His Body, unto Himself at the rapture, and returning with His church in glory, will establish His millennial kingdom on earth ([Acts 1:9-11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%201.9-11); [1 Thessalonians 4:13-18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Thess%204.13-18); Revelation 20).
We teach that the Lord Jesus Christ is the One through whom God will judge all mankind ([John 5:22-23](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%205.22-23)):

items: Believers ([1 Corinthians 3:10-15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%203.10-15); [2 Corinthians 5:10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%205.10))
Living inhabitants of the earth at His glorious return ([Matthew 25:31-46](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2025.31-46))
Unbelieving dead at the Great White Throne ([Revelation 20:11-15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.11-15))

blocks.text: As the Mediator between God and man ([1 Timothy 2:5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Tim%202.5)), the Head of His Body the church ([Ephesians 1:22](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%201.22); [5:23](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ephesians%205.23); [Colossians 1:18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Col%201.18)), and the coming universal King, who will reign on the throne of David ([Isaiah 9:6](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Isa%209.6); [Luke 1:31-33](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Luke%201.31-33)), He is the final Judge of all who fail to place their trust in Him as Lord and Savior ([Matthew 25:14-46](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2025.14-46); [Acts 17:30-31](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%2017.30-31)).

**God the Holy Spirit.** We teach that the Holy Spirit is a divine Person, eternal, underived, possessing all the attributes of personality and deity, including intellect ([1 Corinthians 2:10-13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%202.10-13)), emotions ([Ephesians 4:30](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%204.30)), will ([1 Corinthians 12:11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2012.11)), eternality ([Hebrews 9:14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%209.14)), omnipresence ([Psalm 139:7-10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ps%20139.7-10)), omniscience ([Isaiah 40:13-14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Isa%2040.13-14)), omnipotence ([Romans 15:13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%2015.13)), and truthfulness ([John 16:13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2016.13)). In all the divine attributes He is coequal and consubstantial with the Father and the Son ([Matthew 28:19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2028.19); [Acts 5:3-4](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%205.3-4); [28:25-26](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%2028.25-26); [1 Corinthians 12:4-6](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2012.4-6); [2 Corinthians 13:14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%2013.14); [Jeremiah 31:31-34](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Jer%2031.31-34) with [Hebrews 10:15-17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%2010.15-17)).

We teach that it is the work of the Holy Spirit to execute the divine will with relation to all mankind. We recognize His sovereign activity in creation ([Genesis 1:2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Gen%201.2)), the incarnation ([Matthew 1:18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%201.18)), the written revelation ([2 Peter 1:20-21](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Pet%201.20-21)), and the work of salvation ([John 3:5-7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%203.5-7)).

We teach that the work of the Holy Spirit in this age began at Pentecost, when He came from the Father as promised by Christ ([John 14:16-17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2014.16-17); [15:26](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2015.26)) to initiate and complete the building of the Body of Christ, which is His church ([1 Corinthians 12:13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2012.13)). The broad scope of His divine activity includes convicting the world of sin, of righteousness, and of judgment; glorifying the Lord Jesus Christ and transforming believers into the image of Christ ([John 16:7-9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2016.7-9); [Acts 1:5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%201.5); [2:4](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%202.4); [Romans 8:29](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%208.29); [2 Corinthians 3:18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%203.18); [Ephesians 2:22](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%202.22)).

We teach that the Holy Spirit is the supernatural and sovereign Agent in regeneration, baptizing all believers into the Body of Christ ([1 Corinthians 12:13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2012.13)). The Holy Spirit also indwells, sanctifies, instructs, empowers them for service, and seals them unto the day of redemption ([Romans 8:9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%208.9); [2 Corinthians 3:6](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%203.6); [Ephesians 1:13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%201.13)).

We teach that the Holy Spirit is the divine Teacher, who guided the apostles and prophets into all truth as they committed to writing God’s revelation, the Bible ([2 Peter 1:19-21](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Pet%201.19-21)). Every believer possesses the indwelling presence of the Holy Spirit from the moment of salvation, and it is the duty of all those born of the Spirit to be filled with (controlled by) the Spirit ([John 16:13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2016.13); [Romans 8:9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%208.9); [Ephesians 5:18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%205.18); [1 John 2:20](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20John%202.20), [27](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20John%202.27)).

We teach that the Holy Spirit administers spiritual gifts to the church. The Holy Spirit glorifies neither Himself nor His gifts by ostentatious displays, but He does glorify Christ by implementing His work of redeeming the lost and building up believers in the most holy faith ([John 16:13-14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2016.13-14); [Acts 1:8](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%201.8); [1 Corinthians 12:4-11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2012.4-11); [2 Corinthians 3:18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%203.18)).

We teach, in this respect, that God the Holy Spirit is sovereign in the bestowing of all His gifts for the perfecting of the saints today, and that speaking in tongues and the working of sign miracles in the beginning days of the church were for the purpose of pointing to and authenticating the apostles as revealers of divine truth, and were never intended to be characteristic of the lives of believers ([1 Corinthians 12:4-11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2012.4-11); [13:8-10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Corinthians%2013.8-10); [2 Corinthians 12:12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%2012.12); [Ephesians 4:7-12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%204.7-12); [Hebrews 2:1-4](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%202.1-4)).
Man

We teach that man was directly and immediately created by God in His image and likeness. Man was created free of sin with a rational nature, intelligence, volition, self-determination, and moral responsibility to God ([Genesis 2:7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Gen%202.7), [15-25](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Genesis%202.15-25); [James 3:9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/James%203.9)).

Man was also created by God as either male or female, biologically defined and distinct sexes ([Genesis 1:27](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Gen%201.27); [2:5-23](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Genesis%202.5-23); [1 Corinthians 11:11-15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2011.11-15); [Romans 1:26-27](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%201.26-27)) set by God for each individual ([Psalm 139:13-14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ps%20139.13-14)). Confusion between the two is an abomination to Him ([Leviticus 18:22](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Lev%2018.22); [Deuteronomy 22:5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Deut%2022.5); [Romans 1:26-27](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%201.26-27); [1 Corinthians 6:9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%206.9)).

We teach that God’s intention in the creation of man was that man should glorify God, enjoy God’s fellowship, live his life in the will of God, and by this accomplish God’s purpose for man in the world ([Isaiah 43:7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Isa%2043.7); [Colossians 1:16](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Col%201.16); [Revelation 4:11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%204.11)).

We teach that in Adam’s sin of disobedience to the revealed will and Word of God, man lost his innocence, incurred the penalty of spiritual and physical death, became subject to the wrath of God, and became inherently corrupt and utterly incapable of choosing or doing that which is acceptable to God apart from divine grace. With no recuperative powers to enable him to recover himself, man is hopelessly lost. Man’s salvation is thereby wholly of God’s grace through the redemptive work of our Lord Jesus Christ ([Genesis 2:16-17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Gen%202.16-17); [3:1-19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Genesis%203.1-19); [John 3:36](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%203.36); [Romans 3:23](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%203.23); [6:23](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Romans%206.23); [1 Corinthians 2:14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%202.14); [Ephesians 2:1-3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%202.1-3); [1 Timothy 2:13-14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Tim%202.13-14); [1 John 1:8](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20John%201.8)).

We teach that, because all men were in Adam, a nature corrupted by Adam’s sin has been transmitted to all men of all ages, Jesus Christ being the only exception. All men are thus sinners by nature, by choice, and by divine declaration ([Psalm 14:1-3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ps%2014.1-3); [Jeremiah 17:9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Jer%2017.9); [Romans 3:9-18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%203.9-18), [23](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Romans%203.23); [5:10-12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Romans%205.10-12)).
Salvation

We teach that salvation is wholly of God by grace on the basis of the redemption of Jesus Christ, the merit of His shed blood, and not on the basis of human merit or works ([John 1:12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%201.12); [Ephesians 1:7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%201.7); [2:8-10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ephesians%202.8-10); [1 Peter 1:18-19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Pet%201.18-19)).

**Regeneration.** We teach that regeneration is a supernatural work of the Holy Spirit by which the divine nature and divine life are given ([John 3:3-7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%203.3-7); [Titus 3:5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Titus%203.5)). It is instantaneous and is accomplished solely by the power of the Holy Spirit through the instrumentality of the Word of God ([John 5:24](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%205.24)) when the repentant sinner, as enabled by the Holy Spirit, responds in faith to the divine provision of salvation. Genuine regeneration is manifested by fruits worthy of repentance as demonstrated in righteous attitudes and conduct. Good works are the proper evidence and fruit of regeneration ([1 Corinthians 6:19-20](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%206.19-20); [Ephesians 2:10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%202.10)), and will be experienced to the extent that the believer submits to the control of the Holy Spirit in his life through faithful obedience to the Word of God ([Ephesians 5:17-21](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%205.17-21); [Philippians 2:12b](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Phil%202.12b); [Colossians 3:16](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Col%203.16); [2 Peter 1:4-10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Pet%201.4-10)). This obedience causes the believer to be increasingly conformed to the image of our Lord Jesus Christ ([2 Corinthians 3:18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%203.18)).

Such a conformity is climaxed in the believer’s glorification at Christ’s coming ([Romans 8:17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%208.17); [2 Peter 1:4](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Pet%201.4); [1 John 3:2-3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20John%203.2-3)).

**Election.** We teach that election is the act of God by which, before the foundation of the world, He chose in Christ those whom He graciously regenerates, saves, and sanctifies ([Romans 8:28-30](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%208.28-30); [Ephesians 1:4-11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%201.4-11); [2 Thessalonians 2:13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Thess%202.13); [2 Timothy 2:10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Tim%202.10); [1 Peter 1:1-2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Pet%201.1-2)).

We teach that sovereign election does not contradict or negate the responsibility of man to repent and trust Christ as Savior and Lord ([Ezekiel 18:23](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ezek%2018.23), [32](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ezekiel%2018.32); [33:11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ezekiel%2033.11); [John 3:18-19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%203.18-19), [36](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%203.36); [5:40](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%205.40); [Romans 9:22-23](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%209.22-23); [2 Thessalonians 2:10-12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Thess%202.10-12); [Revelation 22:17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2022.17)). Nevertheless, since sovereign grace includes the means of receiving the gift of salvation as well as the gift itself, sovereign election will result in what God determines. All whom the Father calls to Himself will come in faith, and all who come in faith the Father will receive ([John 6:37-40](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%206.37-40), [44](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%206.44); [Acts 13:48](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%2013.48); [James 4:8](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/James%204.8)).

We teach that the unmerited favor that God grants to totally depraved sinners is not related to any initiative of their own part or to God’s anticipation of what they might do by their own will, but is solely of His sovereign grace and mercy ([Ephesians 1:4-7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%201.4-7); [Titus 3:4-7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Titus%203.4-7); [1 Peter 1:2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Pet%201.2)).

We teach that election should not be looked upon as based merely on abstract sovereignty. God is truly sovereign, but He exercises this sovereignty in harmony with His other attributes, especially His omniscience, justice, holiness, wisdom, grace, and love ([Romans 9:11-16](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%209.11-16)). This sovereignty will always exalt the will of God in a manner totally consistent with His character as revealed in the life of our Lord Jesus Christ ([Matthew 11:25-28](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2011.25-28); [2 Timothy 1:9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Tim%201.9)).

**Justification.** We teach that justification before God is an act of God ([Romans 8:33](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%208.33)) by which He declares righteous those who, through faith in Christ, repent of their sins ([Luke 13:3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Luke%2013.3); [Acts 2:38](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%202.38); [3:19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%203.19); [11:18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%2011.18); [Romans 2:4](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%202.4); [2 Corinthians 7:10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%207.10); [Isaiah 55:6-7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Isa%2055.6-7)) and confess Him as sovereign Lord ([Romans 10:9-10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%2010.9-10); [1 Corinthians 12:3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2012.3); [2 Corinthians 4:5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%204.5); [Philippians 2:11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Phil%202.11)). This righteousness is apart from any virtue or work of man ([Romans 3:20](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%203.20); [4:6](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Romans%204.6)) and involves the imputation of our sins to Christ ([Colossians 2:14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Col%202.14); [1 Peter 2:24](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Pet%202.24)) and the imputation of Christ’s righteousness to us ([1 Corinthians 1:30](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%201.30); [2 Corinthians 5:21](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%205.21)). By this means God is enabled to “be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus” ([Romans 3:26](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%203.26)).

**Sanctification.** We teach that every believer is sanctified (set apart) unto God by justification and is therefore declared to be holy and is therefore identified as a saint. This sanctification is positional and instantaneous and should not be confused with progressive sanctification. This sanctification has to do with the believer’s standing, not his present walk or condition ([Acts 20:32](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%2020.32); [1 Corinthians 1:2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%201.2), [30](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Corinthians%201.30); [6:11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Corinthians%206.11); [2 Thessalonians 2:13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Thess%202.13); [Hebrews 2:11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%202.11); [3:1](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Hebrews%203.1); [10:10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Hebrews%2010.10), [14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Hebrews%2010.14); [13:12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Hebrews%2013.12); [1 Peter 1:2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Pet%201.2)).

We teach that there is also, by the work of the Holy Spirit, a progressive sanctification by which the state of the believer is brought closer to the standing the believer positionally enjoys through justification. Through obedience to the Word of God and the empowering of the Holy Spirit, the believer is able to live a life of increasing holiness in conformity to the will of God, becoming more and more like our Lord Jesus Christ ([John 17:17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2017.17), [19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2017.19); [Romans 6:1-22](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%206.1-22); [2 Corinthians 3:18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%203.18); [1 Thessalonians 4:3-4](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Thess%204.3-4); [5:23](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Thessalonians%205.23)).

In this respect, we teach that every saved person is involved in a daily conflict—the new creation in Christ doing battle against the flesh—but adequate provision is made for victory through the power of the indwelling Holy Spirit. The struggle nevertheless stays with the believer all through this earthly life and is never completely ended. All claims to the eradication of sin in this life are unscriptural. Eradication of sin is not possible, but the Holy Spirit does provide for victory over sin ([Galatians 5:16-25](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Gal%205.16-25); [Ephesians 4:22-24](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%204.22-24); [Philippians 3:12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Phil%203.12); [Colossians 3:9-10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Col%203.9-10); [1 Peter 1:14-16](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Pet%201.14-16); [1 John 3:5-9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20John%203.5-9)).

**Security.** We teach that all the redeemed, once saved, are kept by God’s power and are thus secure in Christ forever ([John 5:24](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%205.24); [6:37-40](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%206.37-40); [10:27-30](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2010.27-30); [Romans 5:9-10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%205.9-10); [8:1](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Romans%208.1), [31-39](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Romans%208.31-39); [1 Corinthians 1:4-8](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%201.4-8); [Ephesians 4:30](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%204.30); [Hebrews 7:25](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%207.25); [13:5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Hebrews%2013.5); [1 Peter 1:5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Pet%201.5); [Jude 24](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Jude%2024)).

We teach that it is the privilege of believers to rejoice in the assurance of their salvation through the testimony of God’s Word, which, however, clearly forbids the use of Christian liberty as an occasion for sinful living and carnality ([Romans 6:15-22](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%206.15-22); [13:13-14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Romans%2013.13-14); [Galatians 5:13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Gal%205.13), [25-26](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Galatians%205.25-26); [Titus 2:11-14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Titus%202.11-14)).

**Separation.** We teach that separation from sin is clearly called for throughout the Old and New Testaments, and that the Scriptures clearly indicate that in the last days apostasy and worldliness shall increase ([2 Corinthians 6:14-7:1](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%206.14-7.1); [2 Timothy 3:1-5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Tim%203.1-5)).

We teach that, out of deep gratitude for the undeserved grace of God granted to us, and because our glorious God is so worthy of our total consecration, all the saved should live in such a manner as to demonstrate our adoring love to God and so as not to bring reproach upon our Lord and Savior. We also teach that separation from all religious apostasy and worldly and sinful practices is commanded of us by God ([Romans 12:1-2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%2012.1-2), [1 Corinthians 5:9-13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%205.9-13); [2 Corinthians 6:14-7:1](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%206.14-7.1); [1 John 2:15-17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20John%202.15-17); [2 John 9-11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20John%209-11)).

We teach that believers should be separated unto our Lord Jesus Christ ([2 Thessalonians 1:11-12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Thess%201.11-12); [Hebrews 12:1-2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%2012.1-2)) and affirm that the Christian life is a life of obedient righteousness that reflects the teaching of the Beatitudes ([Matthew 5:2-12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%205.2-12)) and a continual pursuit of holiness ([Romans 12:1-2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%2012.1-2); [2 Corinthians 7:1](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%207.1); [Hebrews 12:14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%2012.14); [Titus 2:11-14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Titus%202.11-14); [1 John 3:1-10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20John%203.1-10)).
The Church

We teach that all who place their faith in Jesus Christ are immediately placed by the Holy Spirit into one united spiritual Body, the church ([1 Corinthians 12:12-13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2012.12-13)), the bride of Christ ([2 Corinthians 11:2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%2011.2); [Ephesians 5:23-32](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%205.23-32); [Revelation 19:7-8](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2019.7-8)), of which Christ is the Head ([Ephesians 1:22](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%201.22); [4:15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ephesians%204.15); [Colossians 1:18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Col%201.18)).

We teach that the formation of the church, the Body of Christ, began on the Day of Pentecost ([Acts 2:1-21](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%202.1-21), [38-47](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%202.38-47)) and will be completed at the coming of Christ for His own at the rapture ([1 Corinthians 15:51-52](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2015.51-52); [1 Thessalonians 4:13-18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Thess%204.13-18)).

We teach that the church is thus a unique spiritual organism designed by Christ, made up of all born-again believers in this present age ([Ephesians 2:11-3:6](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%202.11-3.6)). The church is distinct from Israel ([1 Corinthians 10:32](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2010.32)), a mystery not revealed until this age ([Ephesians 3:1-6](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%203.1-6); [5:32](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ephesians%205.32)).

We teach that the establishment and continuity of local churches is clearly taught and defined in the New Testament Scriptures ([Acts 14:23](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%2014.23), [27](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%2014.27); [20:17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%2020.17), [28](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%2020.28); [Galatians 1:2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Gal%201.2); [Philippians 1:1](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Phil%201.1); [1 Thessalonians 1:1](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Thess%201.1); [2 Thessalonians 1:1](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Thess%201.1)) and that the members of the one spiritual Body are directed to associate themselves together in local assemblies ([1 Corinthians 11:18-20](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2011.18-20); [Hebrews 10:25](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%2010.25)).

We teach that the one supreme authority for the church is Christ ([1 Corinthians 11:3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2011.3); [Ephesians 1:22](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%201.22); [Colossians 1:18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Col%201.18)) and that church leadership, gifts, order, discipline, and worship are all appointed through His sovereignty as found in the Scriptures. The biblically designated officers serving under Christ and over the assembly are elders (also called bishops, pastors, and pastorteachers; [Acts 20:28](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%2020.28); [Ephesians 4:11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%204.11)) and deacons, both of whom must meet biblical qualifications ([1 Timothy 3:1-13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Tim%203.1-13); [Titus 1:5-9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Titus%201.5-9); [1 Peter 5:1-5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Pet%205.1-5)).

We teach that these leaders lead or rule as servants of Christ ([1 Timothy 5:17-22](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Tim%205.17-22)) and have His authority in directing the church. The congregation is to submit to their leadership ([Hebrews 13:7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%2013.7), [17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Hebrews%2013.17)).

We teach the importance of discipleship ([Matthew 28:19-20](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2028.19-20); [2 Timothy 2:2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Tim%202.2)), mutual accountability of all believers to each other ([Matthew 18:5-14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2018.5-14)), as well as the need for discipline of sinning members of the congregation in accord with the standards of Scripture ([Matthew 18:15-22](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2018.15-22); [Acts 5:1-11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%205.1-11); [1 Corinthians 5:1-13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%205.1-13); [2 Thessalonians 3:6-15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Thess%203.6-15); [1 Timothy 1:19-20](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Tim%201.19-20); [Titus 1:10-16](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Titus%201.10-16)).

We teach the autonomy of the local church, free from any external authority or control, with the right of self-government and freedom from the interference of any hierarchy of individuals or organizations ([Titus 1:5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Titus%201.5)). We teach that it is scriptural for true churches to cooperate with each other for the presentation and propagation of the faith. Each local church, however, through its elders and their interpretation and application of Scripture, should be the sole judge of the measure and method of its cooperation. The elders should determine all other matters of membership, policy, discipline, benevolence, and government as well ([Acts 15:19-31](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%2015.19-31); [20:28](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%2020.28); [1 Corinthians 5:4-7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%205.4-7), [13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Corinthians%205.13); [1 Peter 5:1-4](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Pet%205.1-4)).

We teach that the purpose of the church is to glorify God ([Ephesians 3:21](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%203.21)) by building itself up in the faith ([Ephesians 4:13-16](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%204.13-16)), by instruction of the Word ([2 Timothy 2:2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Tim%202.2), [15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Timothy%202.15); [3:16-17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Timothy%203.16-17)), by fellowship ([Acts 2:47](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%202.47); [1 John 1:3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20John%201.3)), by keeping the ordinances ([Luke 22:19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Luke%2022.19); [Acts 2:38-42](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%202.38-42)) and by advancing and communicating the gospel to the entire world ([Matthew 28:19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2028.19); [Acts 1:8](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%201.8); [2:42](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%202.42)).

We teach the calling of all saints to the work of service ([1 Corinthians 15:58](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2015.58); [Ephesians 4:12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%204.12); [Revelation 22:12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2022.12)).

We teach the need of the church to cooperate with God as He accomplishes His purpose in the world. To that end, He gives the church spiritual gifts. He gives men chosen for the purpose of equipping the saints for the work of the ministry ([Ephesians 4:7-12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%204.7-12)), and He also gives unique and special spiritual abilities to each member of the Body of Christ ([Romans 12:5-8](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%2012.5-8); [1 Corinthians 12:4-31](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2012.4-31); [1 Peter 4:10-11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Pet%204.10-11)).

We teach that there were two kinds of gifts given the early church: miraculous gifts of divine revelation and healing, given temporarily in the apostolic era for the purpose of confirming the authenticity of the apostles’ message ([Hebrews 2:3-4](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%202.3-4); [2 Corinthians 12:12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%2012.12)); and ministering gifts, given to equip believers for edifying one another. With the New Testament revelation now complete, Scripture becomes the sole test of the authenticity of a man’s message, and confirming gifts of a miraculous nature are no longer necessary to validate a man or his message ([1 Corinthians 13:8-12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2013.8-12)). Miraculous gifts can even be counterfeited by Satan so as to deceive even believers ([1 Corinthians 13:13-14:12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2013.13-14.12); [Revelation 13:13-14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2013.13-14)). The only gifts in operation today are those nonrevelatory equipping gifts given for edification ([Romans 12:6-8](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%2012.6-8)).

We teach that no one possesses the gift of healing today, but that God does hear and answer the prayer of faith and will answer in accordance with His own perfect will for the sick, suffering, and afflicted ([Luke 18:1-6](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Luke%2018.1-6); [John 5:7-9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%205.7-9); [2 Corinthians 12:6-10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%2012.6-10); [James 5:13-16](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/James%205.13-16); [1 John 5:14-15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20John%205.14-15)).

We teach that two ordinances have been committed to the local church: baptism and the Lord’s Supper ([Acts 2:38-42](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%202.38-42)). Christian baptism by immersion ([Acts 8:36-39](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%208.36-39)) is the solemn and beautiful testimony of a believer showing forth his faith in the crucified, buried, and risen Savior, and his union with Him in death to sin and resurrection to a new life ([Romans 6:1-11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%206.1-11)). It is also a sign of fellowship and identification with the visible Body of Christ ([Acts 2:41-42](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%202.41-42)).

We teach that the Lord’s Supper is the commemoration and proclamation of His death until He comes, and should be always preceded by solemn self-examination ([1 Corinthians 11:28-32](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2011.28-32)). We also teach that, whereas the elements of Communion are only representative of the flesh and blood of Christ, participation in the Lord’s Supper is nevertheless an actual communion with the risen Christ, who indwells every believer, and so is present, fellowshipping with His people ([1 Corinthians 10:16](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2010.16)).
Angels

**Holy Angels.** We teach that angels are created beings and are therefore not to be worshiped. Although they are a higher order of creation than man, they are created to serve God and to worship Him ([Luke 2:9-14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Luke%202.9-14); [Hebrews 1:6-7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Heb%201.6-7), [14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Hebrews%201.14); [2:6-7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Hebrews%202.6-7); [Revelation 5:11-14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%205.11-14); [19:10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Revelation%2019.10); [22:9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Revelation%2022.9)).

**Fallen Angels.** We teach that Satan is a created angel and the author of sin. He incurred the judgment of God by rebelling against his Creator ([Isaiah 14:12-17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Isa%2014.12-17); [Ezekiel 28:11-19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ezek%2028.11-19)), by taking numerous angels with him in his fall ([Matthew 25:41](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2025.41); [Revelation 12:1-14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2012.1-14)), and by introducing sin into the human race by his temptation of Eve ([Genesis 3:1-15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Gen%203.1-15)).

We teach that Satan is the open and declared enemy of God and man ([Isaiah 14:13-14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Isa%2014.13-14); [Matthew 4:1-11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%204.1-11); [Revelation 12:9-10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2012.9-10)); that he is the prince of this world, who has been defeated through the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ ([Romans 16:20](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%2016.20)); and that he shall be eternally punished in the lake of fire ([Isaiah 14:12-17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Isa%2014.12-17); [Ezekiel 28:11-19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ezek%2028.11-19); [Matthew 25:41](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2025.41); [Revelation 20:10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.10)).
Last Things

**Death.** We teach that physical death involves no loss of our immaterial consciousness ([Revelation 6:9-11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%206.9-11)), that the soul of the redeemed passes immediately into the presence of Christ ([Luke 23:43](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Luke%2023.43); [Philippians 1:23](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Phil%201.23); [2 Corinthians 5:8](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%205.8)), that there is a separation of soul and body ([Philippians 1:21-24](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Phil%201.21-24)), and that, for the redeemed, such separation will continue until the rapture ([1 Thessalonians 4:13-17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Thess%204.13-17)), which initiates the first resurrection ([Revelation 20:4-6](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.4-6)), when our soul and body will be reunited to be glorified forever with our Lord ([Philippians 3:21](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Phil%203.21); [1 Corinthians 15:35-44](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2015.35-44), [50-54](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Corinthians%2015.50-54)). Until that time, the souls of the redeemed in Christ remain in joyful fellowship with our Lord Jesus Christ ([2 Corinthians 5:8](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%205.8)).

We teach the bodily resurrection of all men, the saved to eternal life ([John 6:39](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%206.39); [Romans 8:10-11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%208.10-11), [19-23](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Romans%208.19-23); [2 Corinthians 4:14](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%204.14)), and the unsaved to judgment and everlasting punishment ([Daniel 12:2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Dan%2012.2); [John 5:29](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%205.29); [Revelation 20:13-15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.13-15)).

We teach that the souls of the unsaved at death are kept under punishment until the second resurrection ([Luke 16:19-26](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Luke%2016.19-26); [Revelation 20:13-15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.13-15)), when the soul and the resurrection body will be united ([John 5:28-29](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%205.28-29)). They shall then appear at the Great White Throne Judgment ([Revelation 20:11-15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.11-15)) and shall be cast into hell, the lake of fire ([Matthew 25:41-46](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2025.41-46)), cut off from the life of God forever ([Daniel 12:2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Dan%2012.2); [Matthew 25:41-46](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2025.41-46); [2 Thessalonians 1:7-9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Thess%201.7-9)).

**The Rapture of the Church.** We teach the personal, bodily return of our Lord Jesus Christ before the seven-year tribulation ([1 Thessalonians 4:16](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Thess%204.16); [Titus 2:13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Titus%202.13)) to translate His church from this earth ([John 14:1-3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2014.1-3); [1 Corinthians 15:51-53](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2015.51-53); [1 Thessalonians 4:15-5:11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Thess%204.15-5.11)) and, between this event and His glorious return with His saints, to reward believers according to their works ([1 Corinthians 3:11-15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%203.11-15); [2 Corinthians 5:10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%205.10)).

**The Tribulation Period.** We teach that immediately following the removal of the church from the earth ([John 14:1-3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2014.1-3); [1 Thessalonians 4:13-18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Thess%204.13-18)) the righteous judgments of God will be poured out upon an unbelieving world ([Jeremiah 30:7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Jer%2030.7); [Daniel 9:27](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Dan%209.27); [12:1](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Daniel%2012.1); [2 Thessalonians 2:7-12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Thess%202.7-12); Revelation 16), and that these judgments will be climaxed by the return of Christ in glory to the earth ([Matthew 24:27-31](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2024.27-31); [25:31-46](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matthew%2025.31-46); [2 Thessalonians 2:7-12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Thess%202.7-12)). At that time the Old Testament and tribulation saints will be raised and the living will be judged ([Daniel 12:2-3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Dan%2012.2-3); [Revelation 20:4-6](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.4-6)). This period includes the seventieth week of Daniel’s prophecy ([Daniel 9:24-27](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Dan%209.24-27); [Matthew 24:15-31](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2024.15-31); [25:31-46](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matthew%2025.31-46)).

**The Second Coming and the Millennial Reign.** We teach that, after the tribulation period, Christ will come to earth to occupy the throne of David ([Matthew 25:31](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2025.31); [Luke 1:31-33](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Luke%201.31-33); [Acts 1:10-11](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%201.10-11); [2:29-30](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Acts%202.29-30)) and establish His messianic kingdom for 1,000 years on the earth ([Revelation 20:1-7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.1-7)). During this time the resurrected saints will reign with Him over Israel and all the nations of the earth ([Ezekiel 37:21-28](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ezek%2037.21-28); [Daniel 7:17-22](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Dan%207.17-22); [Revelation 19:11-16](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2019.11-16)). This reign will be preceded by the overthrow of the Antichrist and the False Prophet, and by the removal of Satan from the world ([Daniel 7:17-27](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Dan%207.17-27); [Revelation 20:1-7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.1-7)).

We teach that the kingdom itself will be the fulfillment of God’s promise to Israel ([Isaiah 65:17-25](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Isa%2065.17-25); [Ezekiel 37:21-28](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ezek%2037.21-28); [Zechariah 8:1-17](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Zech%208.1-17)) to restore them to the land that they forfeited through their disobedience ([Deuteronomy 28:15-68](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Deut%2028.15-68)). The result of their disobedience was that Israel was temporarily set aside ([Matthew 21:43](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2021.43); [Romans 11:1-26](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%2011.1-26)), but will again be awakened through repentance to enter into the land of blessing ([Jeremiah 31:31-34](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Jer%2031.31-34); [Ezekiel 36:22-32](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ezek%2036.22-32); [Romans 11:25-29](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%2011.25-29)).

We teach that this time of our Lord’s reign will be characterized by harmony, justice, peace, righteousness, and long life (Isaiah 11; 65:17-25; [Ezekiel 36:33-38](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ezek%2036.33-38)), and will be brought to an end with the release of Satan ([Revelation 20:7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.7)).

**The Judgment of the Lost.** We teach that following the release of Satan after the 1,000-year reign of Christ ([Revelation 20:7](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.7)), Satan will deceive the nations of the earth and gather them to battle against the saints and the beloved city, at which time Satan and his army will be devoured by fire from heaven ([Revelation 20:9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.9)). Following this, Satan will be thrown into the lake of fire and brimstone ([Matthew 25:41](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2025.41); [Revelation 20:10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.10)), whereupon Christ, who is the Judge of all men ([John 5:22](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%205.22)), will resurrect and judge the great and small at the Great White Throne Judgment.

We teach that this resurrection of the unsaved dead to judgment will be a physical resurrection, whereupon receiving their judgment ([John 5:28-29](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%205.28-29)), they will be committed to an eternal conscious punishment in the lake of fire ([Matthew 25:41](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2025.41); [Revelation 20:11-15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.11-15)).

**Eternity.** We teach that after the closing of the millennium, the temporary release of Satan, and the judgment of unbelievers ([2 Thessalonians 1:9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Thess%201.9); [Revelation 20:7-15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.7-15)), the saved will enter the eternal state of glory with God, after which the elements of this earth are to be dissolved ([2 Peter 3:10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Pet%203.10)) and replaced with a new earth, wherein only righteousness dwells ([Ephesians 5:5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%205.5); [Revelation 20:15](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2020.15); [21:1-27](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Revelation%2021.1-27); [22:1-21](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Revelation%2022.1-21)). Following this, the heavenly city will come down out of heaven ([Revelation 21:2](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rev%2021.2)) and will be the dwelling place of the saints, where they will enjoy forever fellowship with God and one another ([John 17:3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2017.3); Revelation 21-22). Our Lord Jesus Christ, having fulfilled His redemptive mission, will then deliver up the kingdom to God the Father ([1 Corinthians 15:24-28](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2015.24-28)), that in all spheres the triune God may reign forever and ever ([1 Corinthians 15:28](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Cor%2015.28)).
What It Means To Be a Christian

Being a Christian is more than identifying yourself with a particular religion or affirming a certain value system. Being a Christian means you have embraced what the Bible says about God, mankind, and salvation. Consider the following truths found in Scripture.

**God Is Sovereign Creator.** Contemporary thinking says man is the product of evolution. But the Bible says we were created by a personal God to love, serve, and enjoy endless fellowship with Him. The New Testament reveals it was Jesus Himself who created everything ([John 1:3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%201.3); [Colossians 1:16](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Col%201.16)). Therefore, He also owns and rules everything ([Psalm 103:19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ps%20103.19)). That means He has authority over our lives and we owe Him absolute allegiance, obedience, and worship.

**God Is Holy.** God is absolutely and perfectly holy ([Isaiah 6:3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Isa%206.3)), therefore He cannot commit or approve of evil ([James 1:13](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/James%201.13)). God requires holiness of us as well. [First Peter 1:16](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Pet%201.16) says, "You shall be holy, for I am holy."

**Mankind Is Sinful.** According to Scripture, everyone is guilty of sin: "There is no man who does not sin" ([1 Kings 8:46](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Kings%208.46)). That doesn’t mean we’re incapable of performing acts of human kindness. But we’re utterly incapable of understanding, loving, or pleasing God on our own. ([Romans 3:10-12](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%203.10-12)).

**Sin Demands a Penalty.** God’s holiness and justice demand that all sin be punished by eternal death ([Ezekiel 18:4](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ezek%2018.4); [Romans 6:23](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%206.23)). That's why simply changing our patterns of behavior can’t solve our sin problem or eliminate its consequences.

**Jesus Is Lord and Savior.** The New Testament reveals it was Jesus Himself who created everything ([Colossians 1:16](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Col%201.16)). Therefore He owns and rules everything ([Psalm 103:19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Ps%20103.19)). That means He has authority over our lives and we owe Him absolute allegiance, obedience, and worship. [Romans 10:9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%2010.9) says, “If you confess with your mouth Jesus as Lord, and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you shall be saved.” Even though God’s justice demands death for sin, His love has provided a Savior who paid the penalty and died for sinners ([1 Peter 3:18](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Pet%203.18)). Christ’s death satisfied the demands of God’s justice and Christ’s perfect life satisfied the demands of God’s holiness ([2 Corinthians 5:21](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/2%20Cor%205.21)), thereby enabling Him to forgive and save those who place their faith in Him ([Romans 3:26](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Rom%203.26)).

**The Character of Saving Faith.** True faith is always accompanied by repentance from sin. Repentance is agreeing with God that you are sinful, confessing your sins to Him, and making a conscious choice to turn from sin ([Luke 13:3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Luke%2013.3),[5](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Luke%2013.5); [1 Thessalonians 1:9](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20Thess%201.9)) and pursue Christ ([Matthew 11:28-30](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Matt%2011.28-30); [John 17:3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/John%2017.3)) and obedience to Him ([1 John 2:3](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/1%20John%202.3)). It isn’t enough to believe certain facts about Christ. Even Satan and his demons believe in the true God ([James 2:19](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/James%202.19)), but they don’t love and obey Him. True saving faith always responds in obedience ([Ephesians 2:10](https://biblia.com/bible/nasb95/Eph%202.10)).
_If you have questions about how you can become a Christian, or want help in knowing how to live the Christian life, please [get in contact with us](/contact-us-2/)._

lede: Beyond mere affiliation, being a Christian is an embodiment of the divine truths enshrined in the Bible. Join us as we explore the foundational principles that define our faith.

blocks.text: **Embracing God's Sovereign Creation:** In a world that champions evolution, the Bible unveils a different truth. We are not accidental outcomes; we are creations lovingly fashioned by a personal God. Jesus Himself is the Creator of all things, signifying His authority over every aspect of our lives (John 1:3; Colossians 1:16).
We owe Him unwavering allegiance, obedience, and worship, for He is the sovereign ruler of all (Psalm 103:19).

**The Holiness of God:** God's holiness is absolute and unblemished (Isaiah 6:3), making Him incapable of condoning evil (James 1:13). This same holiness is expected of us. As 1 Peter 1:16 asserts, "You shall be holy, for I am holy.

**Humanity's Struggle with Sin**: Scripture reveals that all have fallen short and sinned (1 Kings 8:46). While we might exhibit acts of kindness, we remain incapable of understanding, loving, or pleasing God on our own (Romans 3:10-12).
**The Weight of Sin's Consequence:** God's justice demands that sin incurs eternal death (Ezekiel 18:4; Romans 6:23). Mere behavioural change cannot erase our sin problem or its ramifications.

**The Lordship and Salvation of Jesus:** Romans 10:9 declares, "If you confess with your mouth Jesus as Lord and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you shall be saved." Though God's justice necessitates death for sin, His love provided a Savior—Jesus—who bore the penalty for sinners (1 Peter 3:18). Christ's sacrifice satisfied God's justice and holiness, enabling Him to forgive and save those who put their faith in Him (Romans 3:26).

**The Nature of Genuine Faith:** True faith coincides with repentance from sin. Repentance involves acknowledging our sinfulness, confessing our sins, turning away from them (Luke 13:3, 5; 1 Thessalonians 1:9), pursuing Christ (Matthew 11:28-30; John 17:3), and obediently following Him (1 John 2:3). Authentic faith goes beyond acknowledging facts; it responds in loving obedience (Ephesians 2:10).
Discover the Gospel
At Saving Grace Bible Church, we invite you to journey with us to discover the depth and life-transforming essence of the Gospel.

Join us as we delve into the heart of Christian truth and the beauty of the Gospel. At Saving Grace Bible Church, we are a community passionately dedicated to understanding what it means to be a Christian and embracing the life-changing power of the Gospel.
